_comment: UAV model-development direction. Current scientific contract and staged guidance govern iterative implementation; papers support design and novelty comparison.

executorContract.research purpose: Invent, implement and develop defensible new methods for UAV navigation, tracking and exploration. Use accumulated literature to design architectures, learning algorithms and environment-policy training systems. Reproductions and diagnostic pilots are supporting evidence, not the terminal deliverable. Develop a candidate through actual implementation, training when required, and integrated behavior, with novelty judged against architecture-level prior art.
executorContract.presearch policy: Start outside UAV terminology. Build technology cards for predictive representations/JEPA/world models, fast uncertainty and asynchronous paths, memory, planning/control, environment construction, efficient training, and active perception. Transfer is a hypothesis until checked against UAV equivalents.
executorContract.literature policy: Use primary papers, supplements, official project pages, code, datasets, and citation chains. Record exact search boundaries and distinguish exact prior art, functional equivalents, component overlap, adjacent work, and apparently open mechanisms.
executorContract.architecture policy: For each paper record sensors, representation, model role, memory, planner/controller, action interface, training objective, simulator/real setting, latency, compute, and failure modes. VLM/VLA is not an architecture description by itself.
executorContract.experiment policy: Plan matched strong baselines and held-out rendered 3D flight evaluation for the scientific claim. Develop baseline, neural mechanism, training and integration through honest intermediate implementation milestones. State model/data provenance, trained weights, measured timing, current limitations and next milestone. Never call a toy or scripted semantic replacement representative. JSON declarations must be checked against actual code and outputs.
executorContract.compute policy: Scale the faithful method to the RTX 3060 Ti using compact models, frozen backbones, cached features or parameter-efficient training. Keep GPU allocation within the user's 60% VRAM preference (about 4.8 GiB of 8 GiB), measure peak allocated/reserved memory and contention, and adapt batch size before starting. A short smoke test establishes mechanics only; longer training and integrated simulation are allowed without an arbitrary study quota. Report methods requiring unavailable data or larger hardware instead of silently substituting a toy proxy.
executorContract.safety policy: No autonomous physical flight. Start with offline replay, simulation, hardware-in-the-loop, or safe shadow control. Any real test requires a human approval gate and an abort path.
executorContract.novelty policy: Benchmark improvement, prompt change, new dataset, new simulator, backbone swap, or straightforward module composition is not sufficient. The novelty claim must identify a mechanism or interaction absent from the closest functional prior art and state the evidence boundary.
executorContract.invention policy: Develop underlying learned representations, action-conditioned world dynamics, visual judgment/VLM/VLA action computation and shared fast/slow models inside a persistent program. Inspect computational graphs, losses, trainable parameters, data and deployment paths. Use .research-guidance/HANDOFF.md, START.md and original ideas as design sources; they are not proof of novelty. Source review and faithful implementation can proceed together. Continue PROJECT.md and saved model artifacts across tasks. Old toy outcomes are scoped historical records, not model-family rejections.

_literatureAccess: Benchmarks and preprints change quickly. Use the watcher for new leads, but verify important architecture and novelty claims against primary sources, supplements, code, and project pages before recording a synthesis.
